intro: BBC Sport has published a daily quiz titled "Who am I? Guess Premier League star No 13", inviting readers to identify a Premier League player. The short excerpt for the feature challenges participants to work out the identity of the day’s player in as few attempts as possible.

sections.heading: What the BBC Sport "Who am I?" quiz is
sections.text:
The BBC Sport feature is a short, interactive guessing game built around the idea of identifying a Premier League footballer from a series of clues or images. The headline for this instalment makes clear that it is the thirteenth entry in the set: "Who am I? Guess Premier League star No 13." The accompanying excerpt tells players to try to discover the player’s identity in as few attempts as possible, which sets the challenge and format for participation.

This kind of quiz is a familiar format across sports journalism and websites: it mixes fandom, general knowledge and deductive reasoning. The Premier League is the competition in question — a globally followed top-flight league in English football — and the quiz assumes some degree of familiarity with players who compete, or have competed, in that competition. BBC Sport is the platform hosting the game, and its style typically combines accessible clues with a quick, engaging user experience for readers.

sections.heading: How to play and effective guessing strategies
sections.text:
Although the BBC excerpt is brief, the objective is plain: identify the featured Premier League star with the fewest guesses. Players will often be offered a limited number of attempts, progressive hints, or image-based prompts. A sensible approach is to start with broad identifiers — nationality, position or club affiliations commonly associated with well-known Premier League figures — and narrow down only as needed.

Successful guessing in this format depends on balancing risk and information gathering. If the quiz gives visual hints, pay attention to distinctive features like kit colours, squad numbers, or playing style in video clips. When text-based clues are provided, extract keywords and cross-reference them mentally with prominent names that fit those descriptors. If you want to minimise attempts, prioritise players who match multiple likely aspects at once (for example, a high-profile goalkeeper or a long-serving captain), and reserve riskier, obscure guesses for later rounds.

analysis:
This style of short-form quiz works well for casual fans and those who follow the Premier League closely. It encourages engagement, repeat visits and social sharing — readers tend to compare how many attempts they needed and which clues were decisive. From an editorial perspective, rotating a numbered series such as "No 13" keeps the feature fresh while giving readers a predictable format to return to.

For participants, the entertainment value comes as much from the process of elimination as from landing the correct name. While the BBC Sport prompt is deliberately concise, the challenge it poses feeds into broader football culture where recognition and recall of players form a large part of fan identity.
